timeline.title: The idea becomes code
timeline.body: First commit. One server. One goal: every sales channel in a single platform. No investors, no team — just a vision and an empty repository.

timeline.title: Product catalogue
timeline.body: Products. Categories. A first admin interface. The building blocks of any commerce platform, laid down cleanly from the start.

timeline.title: User authentication
timeline.body: Login, sessions, roles. A storefront without authentication is a demo, not a platform. Security-first from week three.

timeline.title: Customers can pay
timeline.body: First checkout flow. Database. A working end-to-end order. A webshop is not a webshop without a pay button — so that came first.

timeline.title: CI/CD from day one
timeline.body: Automated deployment pipeline. Every push triggers a build, a test run, and a deploy to staging. No manual deployments — ever. This discipline has held for every week since.

timeline.title: API layer introduced
timeline.body: A dedicated API Stack repository. Payment providers, webhooks, and external integrations move out of the storefront into their own service. Clean separation from the start.

timeline.title: Stripe integrated
timeline.body: Real payment intents. Webhook verification. Idempotent event handling. Money flows through the platform reliably for the first time.

timeline.title: BUNQ banking connected
timeline.body: Dutch banking integration live. Payment events forwarded to tenants in real time. The API Stack handles its first multi-provider routing.

timeline.title: Multi-tenant foundation
timeline.body: The most important architectural decision: every customer gets their own fully isolated database and environment. No shared tables. No data mixing. This is what makes Pagayo a platform, not a product.

timeline.title: Shared schema package
timeline.body: @pagayo/schema introduced. One set of database definitions, shared across all repositories. A single source of truth — enforced in code, not in documentation.

timeline.title: Design system extracted
timeline.body: @pagayo/design: tokens, components, and context bundles as a standalone package. Every consumer inherits the same visual language. No local overrides.

timeline.title: Shared configuration
timeline.body: @pagayo/config: domains, endpoints, policy, and runtime defaults in one place. Ten repositories, one source of truth for configuration.

timeline.title: First customer live
timeline.body: A real business on their own subdomain. Real orders. Real payments. The platform works — not just in tests, but in production.

timeline.title: POS channel
timeline.body: Point-of-sale flows added alongside the webshop. Same order model, same pipeline, different input surface. The Order-First architecture proves its value for the first time.

timeline.title: Custom domains
timeline.body: Tenants can connect their own domain. Cloudflare for SaaS provisions SSL and routing automatically. No manual DNS configuration. No per-tenant deploy.

timeline.title: One order model for everything
timeline.body: Webshop, POS, WhatsApp, QR — every sales channel flows into a single Order model with a source and an originator. No channel subtypes. No if/else per channel. Order-First.

timeline.title: Edge Workers — core routes
timeline.body: Phase A of the Cloudflare Workers migration complete. Core storefront routes move from a traditional server to the global edge. No infrastructure. No cold starts.

timeline.title: Edge Workers — admin routes
timeline.body: Phase B complete. Admin panel, settings, and tenant management all running on Workers. The last server dependency starts to disappear.

timeline.title: Edge Workers — payment routes
timeline.body: Phase C complete. The full platform runs on Cloudflare Workers. No servers. No VMs. No orchestration. The migration that was planned in months shipped in weeks.

timeline.title: Database at the edge
timeline.body: The database layer was replaced by Cloudflare D1. Every customer gets their own SQLite database, running alongside the Worker — not in a distant data centre. Latency drops. Complexity drops.

timeline.title: Automatic tenant provisioning
timeline.body: New customer? The platform creates a D1 database, applies the full schema, configures Cloudflare routing, and sets up KV cache — all automatically. No deployment. No manual steps.

timeline.title: Subscriptions and memberships
timeline.body: Recurring billing, member management, and visit tracking. Sports clubs, gyms, and membership organisations get a dedicated flow built into the same platform.

timeline.title: Passkey authentication
timeline.body: Passwordless login via WebAuthn. Customers authenticate with Face ID or fingerprint. No passwords to forget, no credentials to breach.

timeline.title: International payment methods
timeline.body: M-Pesa, Flutterwave, and Paystack added. Nigeria, Ghana, South Africa, Kenya — localised payment methods across Europe and Africa, unified in one API layer.

timeline.title: Data migration tooling
timeline.body: Import pipelines for WooCommerce and Magento. Retailers can move their entire catalogue and order history into Pagayo without manual data entry.

timeline.title: Newsletter and announcements
timeline.body: Built-in newsletter tooling with DNS automation. Social announcements. Tenant-to-customer communication without a third-party dependency.

timeline.title: AI layer introduced
timeline.body: AI configuration, action logging, and insight tracking added to the tenant schema. The groundwork for intelligent commerce features — product descriptions, demand forecasting, search.

timeline.title: Today
timeline.body: 2500+ automated deployments. 10 repositories. 59 database tables per tenant. Continuous delivery from the first commit. One developer. Still building.
